title: Synthetic Acceptance Gates and Cost Stability Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines a structured set of synthetic acceptance gates and cost-stability checks used during enterprise onboarding and model cutovers. The goal is to provide deterministic, repeatable validation steps that prove functional correctness, SLO alignment, and cost predictability before a tenant moves to full production traffic.

Scope: Applies to Dedicated and Private tenants and to hosted customers undergoing canary or full cutovers for new model versions, runtime changes (kernel/quantization), or routing policy updates.

When to use this playbook
- New tenant go-lives (first 14 days).
- Model version upgrades that alter tokenization, sampling, or decoding paths.
- Runtime upgrades (quantization profile change, kernel swap, scheduler update).
- Observability or billing pipeline changes that could impact telemetry fidelity.

Key outcomes
- Clear pass/fail criteria for synthetic tests covering correctness, latency, and per-token cost.
- Ownerable rollback/mitigation actions and automated cutover safety nets.
- Actionable signals for QBRs and post-go-live remediation.

Acceptance gates (summary table)
| Gate | Objective | Minimum pass criteria | Primary metric | Tolerance | Owner |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| Functional correctness | Ensure prompts produce expected structured outputs | >= 95% of golden prompts match structure / key fields present | Golden-match-rate | - | CS-Integration + Model-Onboard |
| Latency SLO | Verify p50/p95 token latency within contract SLO | p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 350ms (tenant baseline) | Latency (ms) | p50:+10ms / p95:+50ms | Eng-SRE + Runtime |
| Cost stability | Confirm per-token cost not exceeding baseline by more than threshold | per-token cost delta <= +12% vs baseline (7d) | Per-token-cost (cents) | +12% | FinOps + CS |
| Error & Rate | No increase in request failures or 429s beyond baseline | error-rate delta <= +0.1% absolute, 429s <= baseline*1.5 | error-rate, 429-rate | see tolerance | Support |
| Observability fidelity | Logs, traces, and token-level cost attribution present | 100% telemetry coverage for synthetic requests | telemetry-coverage | 0% tolerance | Telemetry Team |

Detailed procedure (step-by-step)
1) Pre-cutover: prepare tenant baseline (owner: Customer Success engineer)
   a) Capture 7-day baseline: median token cost, latency percentiles, error rates, and golden prompt pass rates. Use the telemetry snapshot tool:

   $ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \n     "https://telemetry.redwood.internal/api/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/baseline?window=7d"

   b) Store baseline as a stable artifact in the tenant onboarding folder and tag it with: baseline:YYYYMMDD.

2) Canary injection: run synthetic suite at increasing traffic levels (owner: Onboarding automation)
   - Phase A: 0.5% of production traffic OR up to 20 rps (whichever is lower) for 30 minutes.
   - Phase B: 2% for 60 minutes.
   - Phase C: 10% for 2 hours (only if A and B pass).

   Synthetic runner configuration (example YAML snippet)

   runner:
     suite_name: "onboard-synthetic-v1"
     concurrency: 4
     ramp: [30, 120, 600] # seconds for phases A,B,C
     sample_set: "tenant-golden-v1.json"
     telemetry_tags: ["onboarding", "tenant:{tenant_id}"]

   Note: YAML above is illustrative — runner accepts JSON or CLI flags. Ensure telemetry_tags include the tenant id for attribution.

3) Synthetic checks (automation)
   - Functional correctness: run golden prompts against the candidate model variant and compute structured field extraction F1 and golden-match-rate. Accept if >= 95%.
   - Latency: compute p50/p95 token latency across synthetic requests. Map percentile anomalies using the runtime profiler.
   - Cost: measure token consumption and billing attribution per synthetic request (includes prefix caching). Compare against baseline.
   - Telemetry: assert logs/traces exist for each synthetic request and that token-level cost tags are present.

4) Automated gate evaluation and alerting
   - The synthetic runner posts results to the onboarding-orchestrator webhook: /onboarding/v1/{tenant_id}/gate-results.
   - If any gate fails, an automated rollback is triggered (see section Rollback & mitigation) and an incident is created in PagerDuty with playbook tag: tenant-onboard-gate-failure.

Rollback & mitigation actions
- Soft rollback: automatically route new requests to previous model variant for 15 minutes while alerting owners. This is fast-fail and requires no manual approval.
- Full rollback: if the soft rollback does not restore metrics within 10 minutes, an auto-change to the previous routing policy is executed and a Severity 2 incident is opened.
- Compensating actions: disable kernel-level optimizations or quantization profile used in the candidate build and re-run Phase A.

Ownership and escalation matrix
- Customer Success (Onboarding): primary owner for test scheduling, baseline capture, and stakeholder comms.
- Eng-SRE: owns latency and runtime performance investigations.
- Runtime Team: owns kernel/quantization mitigations.
- FinOps: validates cost anomalies and approves temporary cost shields.
- PagerDuty escalation: use support-onboard rota; if unresolved for 30 minutes escalate to oncall-lead.

Checklist: pre-cutover (owner: Customer Success)
- [ ] Baseline artifact saved and verified.
- [ ] Synthetic golden set validated and reviewed with customer.
- [ ] Telemetry ingestion confirmed for tenanted tags.
- [ ] Cost attribution hooks enabled (token-level tags).
- [ ] Contact list with 24/7 pager IDs added to onboarding ticket.

Checklist: canary phases (owner: Onboarding automation + SRE)
- [ ] Phase A run complete and gates green.
- [ ] Phase B run complete and gates green.
- [ ] Phase C run complete and gates green (optional).
- [ ] Final go/no-go decision recorded in the onboarding ticket.

Telemetry assertions and sampling guidance
- Required traces: request_id, model_variant, tenant_id, token_count, cache_hit, cost_cents.
- Minimum trace sample rate: 100% for synthetic runner, 1% for production traffic during initial 72 hours after go-live.
- Billing telemetry: ensure per-request cost_cents is emitted and matches billing pipeline within 5% for synthetic traffic.

Integrating with QBRs and health reviews
- Store synthetic-run artifacts as evidence for the first QBR. Include the following in QBR materials:
  - Baseline vs go-live comparison for p50/p95 latency and per-token cost.
  - Golden-match-rate trends for the first 30 days.
  - Any mitigations performed and residual action items.

Common failure modes and workarounds
- Symptom: sudden p95 latency jump during Phase B.
  - Likely causes: kernel swap with unoptimized attention kernel, unexpected batching change.
  - Quick actions: revert kernel flag, increase per-node concurrency limit, re-run Phase A.
- Symptom: per-token cost spike > +12%.
  - Likely causes: cache bypass (prefix mismatch), tokenization change leading to longer sequences.
  - Quick actions: validate tokenization diff tool, enable prefix cache warm-up, engage FinOps to apply temporary cost cap.
- Symptom: missing telemetry or incomplete traces.
  - Workaround: run synthetic runner with telemetry_tags=["onboarding","tenant:{tenant_id}"] and use the telemetry replay tool to re-ingest payloads.

Troubleshooting commands (examples)
- Fetch recent synthetic run results:
  $ rwdctl onboarding runs list --tenant {tenant_id} --limit 10

- Re-run a single golden prompt locally:
  $ rwdctl synth run --tenant {tenant_id} --prompt-file golden/001.json --model variant-a

- Compare tokenization diff:
  $ rwdctl utils token-diff --model-a v1 --model-b v2 --prompt-file golden/001.json

Appendix A: Example golden prompt structure (JSON)
{
  "id": "golden-001",
  "input": "Summarize the following support ticket into category and severity:
> The user's invoice shows incorrect token charges.",
  "expected_fields": {
    "category": "billing",
    "severity": "high"
  }
}

Appendix B: Run frequency and cost guardrails
- Synthetic runner default cadence: run full suite every 6 hours during onboarding.
- Cost budget for synthetic runs: cap at $0.03 per tenant per hour by default. Increase requires FinOps approval.
